program.section_heading: Certificate of Achievement in Deaf Education
outcomes: List strengths and weaknesses of various communication methods currently used with deaf and hard-of-hearing children.
Compare and contrast differing philosophies regarding language options for use with deaf and hard-of-hearing children.
Identify educational placements for deaf and hard-of-hearing children and discuss advantages and disadvantages of each.

notes: Catalog prints codes with hyphens (ASL-140, ASL-145); the closed list stores 'ASL 140' and 'ASL145'. These were treated as the same courses, not catalog additions.
DEAF-330 is printed as an OR option to ASL-140, with its units in parentheses (3.0); recorded as an alternative.
The description says the certificate is awarded for completing 'all six courses', consistent with five required courses plus the ASL-140/DEAF-330 choice totaling 18.0 units.
The career 'cottage counselor' is named in the description as 'employment as a cottage counselor at a school for the deaf'.
The neighboring Deaf Education – Early Intervention Studies and Deaf-Centered Interpreting sections were not read for this record.
